sourcedFrom: Safety & Instruction Manual M&P®10 Semi-Automatic Rifles — p/n 3006082                                                     REV:MP10_082518 (2018)
cleanIntro: The M&P10 field strips on its two receiver pins: push the rear takedown pin, pivot the lower away, and the bolt carrier and charging handle come out of the upper. Deep Clean is Smith & Wesson's own bolt strip, the buffer and spring, the handguard and the magazine.

steps.title: It leaves the factory as a semi-automatic rifle — keep it one
steps.action: Before you take anything off this rifle, understand what changing it means. The M&P10 is sold as a semi-automatic rifle, and end-user changes to its configuration — a pistol barrel under 16 inches on a long gun among them — may bring the firearm under the National Firearms Act with its registration, taxes and other requirements. Complying with federal, state and local law about this rifle and anything you add to it is your responsibility. Note the model and serial number on the lower receiver before you start: Smith & Wesson asks owners to record the serial number before shipping a firearm in for service, and on an NFA-classified configuration the serial number on the registered receiver is the thing the paperwork names.
steps.prose: This is a cleaning bench matter, not just a legal footnote: a strip is exactly when a barrelled upper comes off and a different one goes on, and the manual's own note names that swap. If a shorter upper is going on a lower that has always worn a 16 inch barrel, the paperwork has to exist before the parts meet, not after.
steps.quote: NOTE: The M&P®10, as sold by Smith & Wesson®, is sold as a semi-automatic rifle. Changes to the configuration of the M&P®10 by the end-user, including but not limited to, a pistol barrel (under 16 inches) on a long gun, may subject the firearm to classification under the National Firearms Act, which imposes registration, taxes, and other requirements on the owners of such firearms.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual M&P®10 Semi-Automatic Rifles — p/n 3006082                                                     REV:MP10_082518 — Front matter NOTE, p.2
steps.warn: It is your responsibility to comply with all Federal, state and local laws and regulations regarding the ownership or possession of a firearm such as the M&P®10 and any conversions or additions of any aftermarket accessories to your M&P®10.

steps.title: Magazine out, safety to SAFE, bolt forward
steps.action: Press the magazine release from either side and take the magazine out, then confirm the rifle is not loaded. Place the safety in the SAFE position from either side. If the selector will not rotate easily to SAFE, do not force it — keep the muzzle in a safe direction, remove the magazine and lock the bolt open first, then rotate it to SAFE. Finally, push the top of the bolt release from either side to be sure the bolt is forward.
steps.prose: The safety on an AR-pattern rifle only rotates with the hammer cocked, which is why a rifle whose hammer has been dropped resists — that is the mechanism working, not a fault, and forcing it damages the detent. The bolt goes forward at the end because the takedown that follows wants the carrier home, and the manual warns that the bolt travels forward at considerable speed and force when the release is pressed.
steps.quote: If the safety selector does not easily rotate to the “SAFE” position, DO NOT attempt to force it into “SAFE”. While keeping the muzzle pointed in a safe direction, remove the magazine and lock your bolt open and then rotate the safety selector to “SAFE” before proceeding.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual M&P®10 Semi-Automatic Rifles — p/n 3006082                                                     REV:MP10_082518 — Disassembly / Field Stripping, NOTE, p.24
steps.warn: The bolt moves forward at considerable speed and with considerable force when released by pressing the bolt release. Keep fingers and body parts away from the ejection port at all times as injury may result.

steps.title: Rear takedown pin out to its stop, lower pivoted down
steps.action: Push the takedown pin in from the left side of the receiver — it sits above and behind the trigger — and pull it out on the right side until it comes to a positive stop. Then pivot the lower receiver down and away from the upper.
steps.prose: The pin is captive and stops rather than coming out; do not keep pulling once you feel the stop, because that is what strips the detent. The lower hinges down on the front pivot pin, and if the two halves resist, the buffer retainer is riding on the carrier rather than the pin being stuck.
steps.caution: Never dry-fire with the rifle while it is disassembled. Damage to the rifle will result.
steps.quote: Push in take down pin (above and behind the trigger (FIGURE 54) from left side and pull the pin out on the right side of the receiver until it comes to a positive stop (FIGURE  55).
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual M&P®10 Semi-Automatic Rifles — p/n 3006082                                                     REV:MP10_082518 — Disassembly / Field Stripping, p.25

steps.title: Front pivot pin only if you need the halves apart
steps.action: If you want the upper and lower completely separate, push the pivot pin at the front of the receiver out in the same way as the rear pin and lift the upper off. For most cleaning you do not need to.
steps.prose: Hinged open is enough to reach the bolt carrier, the chamber and the trigger group, and leaving the halves joined means nothing rolls off the bench. Separate them when you want to work on the buffer tube or scrub the lower properly.
steps.quote: If required, remove pivot pin from the front of receiver (FIGURES 57 and 58) in a similar manner to the rear pin and separate the upper receiver from the lower receiver completely.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual M&P®10 Semi-Automatic Rifles — p/n 3006082                                                     REV:MP10_082518 — Disassembly / Field Stripping, p.25

steps.title: Charging handle back, bolt carrier assembly out
steps.action: Pull the charging handle to the rear and draw the bolt carrier assembly out of the upper receiver.
steps.prose: The carrier rides out on the charging handle for the first part of its travel and then comes free in your hand — support it, because a .308 carrier is heavy enough to mark a receiver if it drops back in. Everything you take out here is carbon-coated, so have somewhere to put it.
steps.quote: Pull the charging handle to rear and remove bolt carrier assembly (FIGURE 59).
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual M&P®10 Semi-Automatic Rifles — p/n 3006082                                                     REV:MP10_082518 — Disassembly / Field Stripping, p.25

steps.title: Charging handle back to its takedown notch and down
steps.action: With the carrier out, pull the charging handle backwards to the takedown notch and lift it down and out of the upper receiver.
steps.prose: There is a wide spot part-way along the charging handle's channel and that is the only place it will drop out — pulling it straight back to the end of its travel and tugging will not release it. It goes back in the same way, so remember where that notch was.
steps.quote: Remove charging handle by pulling it backwards to the takedown notch and down out of the upper receiver (FIGURE 60)
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual M&P®10 Semi-Automatic Rifles — p/n 3006082                                                     REV:MP10_082518 — Disassembly / Field Stripping, p.26

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Upper receiver, lower receiver, bolt carrier assembly and charging handle — that is the M&P10 field stripped, and enough to clean the bore, the chamber and the action. Deep Clean carries Smith & Wesson's own bolt strip, the buffer and spring, the handguard and the magazine. Do not dry fire the rifle while it is disassembled.
steps.prose: Note the gas tube discolours from heat and the manual tells you not to try to remove that discolouration — it is not fouling and scrubbing at it achieves nothing.
steps.quote: NEVER DISASSEMBLE YOUR FIREARM BEYOND THE FIELD STRIPPING PROCESS OUTLINED IN THIS MANUAL. NEVER MANIPULATE ANY INTERNAL COMPONENTS BEYOND WHAT YOU ARE SPECIFICALLY INSTRUCTED TO DO IN THIS MANUAL SINCE THIS MAY AFFECT THE RELIABILITY, FUNCTIONING AND SAFETY OF YOUR FIREARM.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual M&P®10 Semi-Automatic Rifles — p/n 3006082                                                     REV:MP10_082518 — Special Component Disassembly, WARNING, p.30

deepSteps.title: Bolt forward to unlocked, firing pin retaining pin out
deepSteps.action: With the bolt carrier out of the rifle, move the bolt forward in the carrier to the unlocked position, then remove the firing pin retaining pin.
deepSteps.prose: The bolt has to be forward or the retaining pin fouls the firing pin's collar and will not come out. That pin is a split cotter and the manual is explicit that its split end must not be altered — squeezing it closed to make it 'fit better' is how it stops holding at all.
deepSteps.caution: Do not alter the split end of the firing pin retaining pin (FIG.
deepSteps.quote: Once the bolt carrier is clear of the firearm, move the bolt forward in the carrier to the unlocked position (FIGURE 64)  and remove the firing pin retaining pin (FIGURE  65).
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual M&P®10 Semi-Automatic Rifles — p/n 3006082                                                     REV:MP10_082518 — Bolt Field Stripping, p.26

deepSteps.title: Bolt back to locked, firing pin out of the rear
deepSteps.action: Push the bolt back into the carrier to put it in the locked position, then take the firing pin out of the rear of the bolt carrier.
deepSteps.prose: This is the reverse of the last step and it catches people: unlocked to free the retaining pin, locked to release the firing pin. With the bolt locked forward the firing pin's tail clears the cam pin and drops out of the back of the carrier under its own weight.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the firing pin out of the rear of the bolt carrier (FIG. 67).
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual M&P®10 Semi-Automatic Rifles — p/n 3006082                                                     REV:MP10_082518 — Bolt Field Stripping, p.27

deepSteps.title: Cam pin out, then the bolt
deepSteps.action: Lift the bolt cam pin out of the bolt carrier, then draw the bolt out of the front of the carrier.
deepSteps.prose: The cam pin only lifts clear when the bolt is rotated to the right position, which the previous step left it in — if it will not come out, turn the bolt a quarter turn and try again rather than pulling harder. Note that the cam pin goes back staked side down; that is the only orientation it will enter.
deepSteps.quote: Lift the bolt cam pin out of the bolt carrier (FIGURE 68).
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual M&P®10 Semi-Automatic Rifles — p/n 3006082                                                     REV:MP10_082518 — Bolt Field Stripping, p.27

deepSteps.title: Extractor out — and leave its spring assembly alone
deepSteps.action: Press in on the extractor while pushing the extractor retaining pin out with a small punch or drift, then take the extractor off the bolt. Do not remove the rubber grommet from the spring, and do not take the extractor or its spring assembly apart.
deepSteps.prose: The extractor spring on a .308 bolt is a captive assembly with an insert that sets the tension, and the manual bars disassembling it outright — pulling that grommet out is how an extractor stops holding a case rim. Clean the extractor and the recess it sits in, then put it straight back.
deepSteps.quote: Press in on the extractor while pushing the extractor retaining pin out with a small punch or drift (FIGURE 70).
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual M&P®10 Semi-Automatic Rifles — p/n 3006082                                                     REV:MP10_082518 — Bolt Field Stripping, p.27
deepSteps.warn: DO NOT DISASSEMBLE THE EXTRACTOR OR THE SPRING ASSEMBLY.

deepSteps.title: Buffer and spring out of the receiver extension
deepSteps.action: Push the buffer in slightly at the rear of the receiver, depress the buffer retainer to release it, and take the buffer and spring out of the buffer tube.
deepSteps.prose: Push in first, then depress the retainer — depressing the retainer with the buffer resting on it does nothing but bend the detent. The spring is long and under load, so keep a hand on the buffer as it comes out; on a .308 there is enough energy there to launch it across a room.
deepSteps.quote: Push in buffer (at the rear of the receiver / front of the stock) slightly and depress buffer retainer to release the buffer (FIG. 72).
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual M&P®10 Semi-Automatic Rifles — p/n 3006082                                                     REV:MP10_082518 — Buffer and Spring / Field Stripping, p.28

deepSteps.title: Handguard: two people, one on the slip ring
deepSteps.action: If the handguard has to come off, stand the rifle on its buttstock with one hand on the stock and the other on the lower end of the handguard. Have a second person pull down on the slip ring with both hands while you pull one side of the handguard free, then repeat for the other side.
deepSteps.prose: Smith & Wesson calls this the buddy system and prints it that way for a reason — the delta ring spring is stiff enough that a single pair of hands cannot hold it down and lever a handguard half out at the same time. Trying it alone with a screwdriver is what cracks handguards and marks the barrel nut.
deepSteps.quote: While your buddy pulls down on the slip ring, which is a two-handed procedure, pull one side of the hand guard free (FIGURES 77 and  78).
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual M&P®10 Semi-Automatic Rifles — p/n 3006082                                                     REV:MP10_082518 — Special Component Disassembly, Handguard Removal, p.29

deepSteps.title: Magazine floorplate, opened with a cartridge tip
deepSteps.action: With the magazine empty, press the floorplate retainer down through the hole in the floorplate using a pointed object — a 308 cartridge tip works. Keep the magazine body pointed away from yourself and others with your thumb over the exposed body, then slide the floorplate off.
deepSteps.prose: A thumb over the opening is what stops the spring leaving with the plate; the manual asks for it explicitly. Take the spring, follower and floorplate retainer out as one assembly and clean the inside of the body — a .308 magazine holds a long, heavy stack and grit in the tube shows up as failures to feed the last rounds.
deepSteps.quote: Using a pointed object (such as a 308 Cartridge), press the floorplate retainer down by passing the bullet tip through the hole in the floorplate (FIG. 90).
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual M&P®10 Semi-Automatic Rifles — p/n 3006082                                                     REV:MP10_082518 — Magazine Disassembly, p.34
deepSteps.warn: Magazine spring is under pressure. Control the spring and the floor plate retainer so that they do not fly out and cause injury.

cleaning.name: BORE AND CHAMBER
tasks: Remove excessive firing residue from the bore and chamber with a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent
Finish by running a dry cotton cloth patch through the bore and chamber to remove residue and solvent
Clean the locking lug recesses in the barrel extension, where carbon packs hardest on a direct-impingement rifle
Remove excess oil, cleaning solution and cleaning materials from the bore — be certain the barrel is clear of obstructions before shooting

cleaning.name: BOLT CARRIER GROUP
tasks: Clean the bolt tail, the gas rings and the inside of the carrier
Clean the bolt face, the extractor recess and the underside of the extractor claw
Clean the firing pin and its channel through the carrier, and dry it rather than flooding it with oil
Do not attempt to remove the discolouration on the gas tube — it comes from heat and is not fouling

cleaning.name: RECEIVERS AND BUFFER
tasks: Clean the upper receiver's interior and the charging handle channel
Clean the lower receiver, the trigger group area and the magazine well
Clean the buffer, the spring and the inside of the buffer tube if they have been removed
Clean the exterior with a non-abrasive cleaning cloth and remove all solution, oil and fingerprints

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Lubricate all metal parts by wiping them with a cloth dampened with a high quality firearm oil, then remove the excess
Leave a light film of oil on all metal parts inside and out
Avoid prolonged solvent immersion and prolonged ultrasonic cleaning
Never use ammoniated or other strong alkaline solvents on this rifle

reassembly: Assemble the rifle in the reverse order that you took it apart.
The bolt cam pin only goes in when the bolt is rotated correctly in the carrier, with the staked side down.
Stagger the gaps on the gas rings so they are NOT aligned with one another — aligned gaps cost you gas seal and reliability.
Refit the buffer and spring, letting the buffer retainer rise to capture the buffer.
Refit the charging handle through its takedown notch first, then run the bolt carrier assembly in behind it, close the lower onto the upper and push the takedown pin home.
Magazine: follower, spring and floorplate retainer back into the body, then the floorplate slid over the tabs until the retainer locks it.
fncheck: With the rifle empty and pointed in a safe direction, check both receiver pins are pushed fully home and the receivers are closed with no gap. Cycle the charging handle several times and confirm the bolt carrier runs fully into battery, the bolt locks, and the bolt catch holds the carrier back on an empty magazine and releases cleanly. Check the safety selector rotates positively between SAFE and FIRE from both sides with the hammer cocked, and that it will not rotate to FIRE without the hammer cocked. Then seat an empty magazine and confirm it latches and drops free.
